thread:
aj: Heads up — during this morning's asia-east1 batch we saw a spike of GPU preempts and the cluster autoscaler failed to route to fallback pools quickly enough. Pod queues grew ~2.5k, a few inference lanes hit latency SLOs.
kevin: Ugh. Was that the new aggressive binpack policy + scaleDownDelay combo?
sophie: Yep. We pushed binpack=high and scaleDownDelaySeconds=300 so nodes stay longer, but when preempts come it blocks rapid refill.
maria: We should have a playbook: (1) detect >X preempts/min, (2) fast-failover to on-demand hot-standby pool, (3) prewarm a small number of nodes with GPU taints, (4) throttle low-priority jobs.
aj: Agreed. Proposal: add a route in smart-routing that prefers "gpu-hot-standby" nodepool when preemptible evictionRate > 0.5 for 1m. Also change CA config for those nodepools to enable faster scale up.
kevin: What config change do you mean? sample?
sophie: e.g. increase maxSurge and reduce targetUtilization for the autoscaler on fallback pools. Also set a separate cluster-autoscaler profile with aggressive scaleUpDelaySec=10 and exponential backoff disabled.
cluster-autoscaler-bot: autofix suggestion: set --scale-up-delay=10s for nodepool=gpu-hot-standby in the CA deployment.
maria: Also want to be careful with cost — continuous hot-standby in us-west would blow monthly spend. Keep standby size at 2-4 GPUs per region and only route traffic when preempt rate threshold crossed.
aj: Right. Default idle policy: 3 nodes prewarmed per critical region, scaleToZero disabled for the pool, tainted with "dedicated=standby:NoSchedule" and label "redwood.priority=hot-standby".
kevin: For draining preempted nodes we should use graceful drain hooks so inference proxies can failover keys and reuse KV caches where possible. Add a pre-drain webhook: /internal/drain-notify -> frontend to requeue.
sophie: Example k8s taint/toleration and autoscaler snippet:
```
# nodepool spec (concept)
nodePool:
  name: gpu-hot-standby
  autoscaling:
    enabled: true
    min: 2
    max: 8
    gpu: true
  taints:
    - key: dedicated
      value: standby
      effect: NoSchedule
# cluster-autoscaler flags per-profile
--scale-up-delay=10s
--scale-down-delay=5m
--node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/redwood:nodepool=gpu-hot-standby
```
maria: Nice. We should also add a routing policy in the inference service to accept a fallback hint header (X-Redwood-Fallback: hot-standby) so the control plane can direct new requests.
aj: Next steps: kevin to open a PR with CA profile + nodepool change, sophie to add routing header + drain webhook, maria to draft cost cap alerting. I'll run a canary in asia-east1 tomorrow 03:00 UTC. @kevin @sophie please coordinate. :rocket:
kevin: On it. Will include a dry-run of 2 nodes and synthetic load to validate scaling time <60s.
sophie: I'll add telemetry (token-level latency + queue depth) to the canary dashboard.
cluster-autoscaler-bot: note: ensure IAM role for auto-provisioning has quota-check permissions in target regions.
aj: Good catch. Also add fallback limits per-customer so one noisy tenant doesn't eat the standby pool.
maria: I'll update the playbook doc in confluence and ping SRE for runbook adjustments.
kevin: Thanks — will post PR link when ready.
aj: :thumbsup:
